svg.title: Reconcile $490,000 Gross to $159,250 Owner Net
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-revenue-to-owner-net; chart type: waterfall; title: Reconcile $490,000 Gross to $159,250 Owner Net; subtitle: Four illustrative cost deductions produce the canonical 32.5% margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: First and last bars are totals; the four intervening bars are negative deductions. Revenue and owner net are canonical; cost category allocations are illustrative. Annual costs total $330,750, or $27,562.50 monthly. The supplied $2,500–$14,000 monthly opex range cannot be an all-in ceiling for this Base case: implied annual costs exceed its $240,000 upper annual equivalent by $90,750. Resolve that scope difference before budgeting.; caption: $490,000 minus $156,000 minus $84,000 minus $42,000 minus $48,750 equals $159,250; $159,250 divided by $490,000 equals 32.5%. Referred merchant sales never enter publisher gross revenue.; stages: label: Publisher gross revenue; value: $490,000 annual recognized operator revenue; numeric value: 490000.0; detail: Illustrative rail allocation is $218,000 advertising, $212,000 approved affiliate commissions, and $60,000 delivered sponsorship revenue; the three components reconcile.; label: Full-time labor; value: Subtract $156,000 in modeled annual labor; numeric value: -156000.0; detail: Allocate $156,000 to the single full-time seat in the 1 FT + 3 C core pod. Treat this as a modeled loaded labor budget, not a salary survey finding or a separate owner distribution.; label: Contracted production; value: Subtract $84,000 in modeled contractor fees; numeric value: -84000.0; detail: The core pod includes three fractional contractor seats, not four. The unchanged $84,000 production envelope covers their purchased capacity and any external vendor/trade sub-crews charged to direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through. External crews are not internal pod headcount; do not add their costs again outside this deduction.; label: Publishing infrastructure; value: Subtract $42,000 in modeled infrastructure costs; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Budget hosting, security maintenance, audit tools, analytics, licensed datasets, and production software. Separate one-time setup purchases from recurring costs to prevent duplication.; label: Commercial and administrative costs; value: Subtract $48,750 in modeled remaining expenses; numeric value: -48750.0; detail: Allocate $24,000 to commercial development, $12,000 to bookkeeping and contract administration, and $12,750 to insurance, banking, and other incurred operating expenses.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $159,250 retained after modeled operating costs; numeric value: 159250.0; detail: Preserve the canonical Base result. Conservative revenue of $80,000 at 20% yields $16,000; Scaled revenue of $900,000 at 45% yields $405,000.

rect.title: label: Publisher gross revenue; value: $490,000 annual recognized operator revenue; numeric value: 490000.0; detail: Illustrative rail allocation is $218,000 advertising, $212,000 approved affiliate commissions, and $60,000 delivered sponsorship revenue; the three components reconcile.

label: Full-time labor; value: Subtract $156,000 in modeled annual labor; numeric value: -156000.0; detail: Allocate $156,000 to the single full-time seat in the 1 FT + 3 C core pod. Treat this as a modeled loaded labor budget, not a salary survey finding or a separate owner distribution.

label: Contracted production; value: Subtract $84,000 in modeled contractor fees; numeric value: -84000.0; detail: The core pod includes three fractional contractor seats, not four. The unchanged $84,000 production envelope covers their purchased capacity and any external vendor/trade sub-crews charged to direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through. External crews are not internal pod headcount; do not add their costs again outside this deduction.

label: Publishing infrastructure; value: Subtract $42,000 in modeled infrastructure costs; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Budget hosting, security maintenance, audit tools, analytics, licensed datasets, and production software. Separate one-time setup purchases from recurring costs to prevent duplication.

label: Commercial and administrative costs; value: Subtract $48,750 in modeled remaining expenses; numeric value: -48750.0; detail: Allocate $24,000 to commercial development, $12,000 to bookkeeping and contract administration, and $12,750 to insurance, banking, and other incurred operating expenses.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $159,250 retained after modeled operating costs; numeric value: 159250.0; detail: Preserve the canonical Base result. Conservative revenue of $80,000 at 20% yields $16,000; Scaled revenue of $900,000 at 45% yields $405,000.

text.title: Assumptions: First and last bars are totals; the four intervening bars are negative deductions. Revenue and owner net are canonical; cost category allocations are illustrative. Annual costs total $330,750, or $27,562.50 monthly. The supplied $2,500–$14,000 monthly opex range cannot be an all-in ceiling for this Base case: implied annual costs exceed its $240,000 upper annual equivalent by $90,750. Resolve that scope difference before budgeting.
